title: Cooperative Exploration in Decentralized Bandit Networks.
journal: Proc. ACM Measure. Anal. Comput. Syst.
kw: We study a decentralized learning problem in which a population of agents repeatedly solves a shared stochastic multi-armed bandit task while exchanging sparse, asynchronous messages over a local communication graph. Each agent chooses an arm, decides whether to communicate, and updates its policy using only its own history together with limited peer observations. We propose a collaborative exploration protocol that shares compact arm summaries rather than raw rewards, enabling reduced regret under constrained bandwidth. The analysis characterizes per-agent regret as a function of the number of agents, the number of arms, the horizon, and the communication sparsity, and compares the method against both fully independent learning and fully connected information sharing. Empirical results on synthetic networked bandit instances show that minimal collaboration can substantially improve sample efficiency without incurring the cost of global synchronization.

title: Adaptive Guardrails for Cloud Scheduling: Prediction-Aware Dispatching Under Heavy Traffic
journal: Proc. ACM Meas. Anal. Comput. Syst.
pb: Association for Computing Machinery, abbreviated ACM
kw: Cloud resource provisioning and load balancing both face volatile demand, where dispatching and scheduling decisions must be made online under uncertainty. Empirical experiments on synthetic and trace-driven workloads show that prediction errors vary by workload class and time horizon, while theoretical bounds demonstrate that the augmented policy remains robust and near-optimal in congested regimes.

journal: Proc. ACM Meas. Anal. Comput. Syst.
kw: Hybrid query processing systems increasingly combine CPU and gPU resources to accelerate large-scale data workflows. This article studies adaptive filtering strategies for join processing when filter selectivity, execution overheads, and hardware placement vary across workloads. We examine how lightweight bloom-style filters can be co-processed with join operators, how stale or low-value filters affect throughput, and how performance changes on resource-constrained systems. Using measurements from representative analytical pipelines, we identify common cases where filtering improves latency but also cases where excessive filtering logic introduces dead weight and degrades execution efficiency. The approach is especially useful for mixed workload environments and distributed data platforms that must balance speed, energy use, and operator complexity.

The platform highlights the convergence of intrinsic sensing, soft materials, and dual-responsive actuation for next-generation adaptive robotic manipulation systems.

title: A hybrid authentication framework for outdoor visible light sensor networks
authors: ['M. R. Solano', ' H. C. Ferreira', ' Priya Nair']
kw: AbstractOutdoor visible light sensor networks combine communication, sensing, and environmental exposure in scenarios such as street lighting, vehicle links, and smart-city monitoring. Compared with indoor deployments, these systems face higher interference, variable illumination, weather-driven attenuation, and stronger security risks due to open-channel operation. This article proposes a hybrid authentication and key agreement framework tailored to outdoor VLC-enabled sensor networks. The scheme integrates lightweight mutual authentication, replay resistance, device compromise mitigation, and traceability protection while preserving low communication and computational overhead. Formal verification is provided using ProVerif, and performance is assessed against related protocols in terms of message complexity, storage cost, and security properties. The study also discusses deployment considerations for fog, rain, haze, and solar-powered receivers, and identifies research opportunities for resilient Li-Fi based sensing infrastructures.

title: Self-attention guided deep network for multimodal NER in Chinese clinical records
authors: Yifan Zhou, Mengfei Li, and Jie Chen
journal: BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making
pb: Business Science and Springer Media LLC
kw:
Abstract
Background
Deep learning methods have shown strong performance in named entity recognition for Chinese clinical records, but heterogeneous document structure and overlapping medical expressions remain challenging. In particular, combining token-level context with modality-aware attention can improve the extraction of diagnoses, symptoms, and treatments from electronic medical records.

Methods
We propose a self-attention guided deep network that integrates part-of-speech features and multimodal clinical context. The model uses a dual-path encoder to capture character and word representations, followed by an adaptive attention fusion module to emphasize clinically informative spans across structured notes and narrative text. A conditional decoding layer is applied to generate entity labels for medical named entity recognition.

Results
Experiments on a Chinese electronic medical record corpus show improved precision, recall, and F1 score over baseline BiLSTM-CRF and attention-only systems. The model performs particularly well on disease and examination entities while maintaining stable results across longer discharge summaries.

Conclusions
The proposed method demonstrates that self-attention and modality-aware fusion can enhance named entity recognition in Chinese medical text, supporting downstream information extraction in clinical decision support systems.

title: A hybrid reliability assessment framework for two-phase degradation systems using intuitionistic fuzzy optimization
kw: AbstractA hybrid methodology is proposed to improve the reliability assessment of two-phase degradation systems when the change point is uncertain and expert judgments are imprecise. The framework combines heuristic linear programming with triangular intuitionistic fuzzy numbers to derive feasible priority rankings for critical failure modes and intervention actions. A Wiener-process degradation model is used to represent the evolving system condition, while Spearman correlation is applied to evaluate the stability of the resulting rankings. A numerical case study demonstrates that the proposed approach produces consistent and robust safety decisions compared with conventional probabilistic methods, particularly when the available data are sparse and subjective assessments are ambiguous.

title: Comparative Analysis of Sampling Schemes for Event-Based Landslide Susceptibility Mapping with Recurrent Neural Networks
kw: This study compares multiple sampling schemes for event-based landslide susceptibility mapping using recurrent neural networks, focusing on how inventory construction and class balance affect predictive stability. The experiment examines source and run-out landslide representations, evaluates hybrid and spatially stratified sampling, and tests cost-sensitive training to reduce false alarms and omission errors. A typhoon-triggered landslide dataset from southern Taiwan is used to assess model robustness under different preprocessing settings. Results indicate that separating run-out areas as an independent class improves classification consistency, while balanced sampling generally yields higher overall accuracy and kappa than naive random sampling. The paper highlights the importance of aligning sampling design with geomorphic heterogeneity when building data-driven susceptibility models.
